entities.summary:
Gaetano dei Conti di Thiene, known in English as Saint Cajetan, was an Italian Catholic priest and religious reformer, co-founder of the Theatines. Born around 1480 in Thiene, Italy, he died on August 17, 1547. He became a prominent figure in the Counter-Reformation, advocating for the restoration of Catholic doctrine and practices. Saint Cajetan's reforming efforts focused on the spiritual renewal of laypeople, particularly through the establishment of Theatine monasteries and the development of the 'Theatine Rule.' This led to the growth of the Theatine Order, with over 1,000 monasteries across Europe by the end of the 16th century. His commitment to the spiritual transformation of humanity resonated with the intellectual and cultural climate of 16th-century Europe, where the tensions between Catholicism and Protestantism were at their peak. As a result, Saint Cajetan's influence can be seen in the ongoing Catholic-Protestant debates and the emergence of new Catholic orders during the Reformation period.

He is recognised as a saint in the Catholic Church, and his feast day is 7 August. His legacy extends beyond the religious sphere, as he played a crucial role in shaping the cultural and intellectual landscape of 16th-century Italy. The Theatine Rule, which he helped develop, continues to be studied by scholars of Catholicism and Christian spirituality today.

Saint Cajetan's spiritual and reforming efforts also had a profound impact on the lives of ordinary people, particularly the poor and marginalized. His emphasis on the importance of prayer, penance, and charity helped to create a sense of community and shared purpose among the faithful. This, in turn, contributed to the growth of a more compassionate and inclusive form of Christianity, which would go on to shape the course of Western religious history.
